title: Live updates: Jury finds Miguel Olivares guilty of first-degree murder in Faith Hedgepeth death
text:
Faith Hedgepeth Murder: Miguel Olivares' trial enters closing arguments, jury deliberations, verdict phase in UNC student's death - ABC11 Raleigh-Durham 
 24/7 Live Raleigh Durham Fayetteville Surrounding Area Live Faith Hedgepeth 
 Live updates: Jury finds Miguel Olivares guilty of first-degree murder in Faith Hedgepeth death 
 Last updated: Friday, October 23, 2026 9:03PM GMT Share DURHAM, N.C. (WTVD) -- The defense for Miguel Salguero Olivares , the man accused of killing UNC student Faith Hedgepeth , rested its case Wednesday without presenting evidence or calling a single witness .
 Before the defense rested, Olivares told the judge he would not testify in his own defense. The case now moves to closing arguments starting Thursday.
 The judge dismissed jurors for the day Wednesday before meeting with prosecutors and defense attorneys to discuss closing arguments.
 Prosecutors rested their case Monday, Oct. 19, after nine days of testimony. In all, the state called 23 witnesses, including forensic experts from the North Carolina State Crime Lab, Hedgepeth's former roommate and SBI agents.
 Olivares' trial came fourteen years after UNC student Faith Hedgepeth was found murdered in her apartment in Chapel Hill and five years after he was charged with the crime.

 Jury has reached a verdict in the Faith Hedgepeth murder trial 
 BREAKING: Jury finds Miguel Salguero-Olivares guilty on all counts in Faith Hedgepeth murder trial
 The jury has reached a verdict in the trial of Miguel Salguero Olivares, finding him guilty on all counts. Jurors convicted him of first-degree murder, first-degree burglary, first-degree rape and a first-degree sexual offense in the 2012 death of Faith Hedgepeth.
 37 minutes ago 
 Jury finds Miguel Olivares guilty of all 4 counts in the murder of Faith Hedgepeth 
 On Friday, just before 4:30 pm., the jury informed the court they had reached a verdict.
 They found Miguel Salguero Olivares guilty on all four counts of:
 Miguel Salguero Olivares on Friday, Oct.23, 2026, after the jury reads the verdict finding him guilty on four counts. 
 Guilty of first-degree murder
 Guilty of first-degree rape
 Guilty of first-degree burglary
 Guilty of first-degree sexual offense
 The state presented nine days of evidence and called 23 witnesses, including Hedgepeth's former roommate, other former friends, forensic experts, and SBI agents.
 1 hour and 29 minutes ago 
 Here are the 4 charges jurors in Faith Hedgepeth murder trial are deliberating 
 After 14 years of questions surrounding the death of UNC-Chapel Hill sophomore Faith Hedgepeth , the case against Miguel Salguero Olivares is now in the hands of a jury.
 Jurors received their instructions and started deliberating late Thursday and a few hours later, the court recessed.
 "I don't think there's going to be a rush for a judgment here in this case," North Carolina Central University School of Law Professor Irving Joyner told ABC11 on Thursday.
 Joyner said jurors must carefully evaluate the evidence within the framework of the judge's instructions.
 Jurors asked for the DNA reports and received them Friday morning before they resumed deliberations.
 The state presented nine days of evidence and called 23 witnesses, including Hedgepeth's former roommate, other former friends, forensic experts, and SBI agents.
 2:01 PM GMT 
 Jurors receive DNA reports they requested, now resuming deliberations 
 Before ending their first day of deliberations on Thursday, jurors requested summaries of latent fingerprint and DNA reports introduced during the trial.
 Friday morning, Judge Gregory granted the request, and they received the reports.
 Judge Gregory speaks with jurors on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, about their request for DNA reports Jurors then returned to their room to continue deliberations.
 Jurors began deliberating Thursday afternoon in the murder trial of Miguel Salguero Olivares following emotional and often contentious closing arguments from both sides. There were tears and hugs inside the courtroom as the case was finally handed to the jury.
 Follow along in our live blog .
 1:25 PM GMT 
 Faith Hedgepeth murder: Jurors continue deliberations 
 After 14 years of questions surrounding the death of UNC-Chapel Hill sophomore Faith Hedgepeth , the case against Miguel Salguero Olivares is now in the hands of a jury.
 Closing arguments concluded Thursday, and jurors began deliberating that afternoon before being sent home shortly after 5 p.m.
 Prosecutors argued that forensic evidence overwhelmingly points to Olivares as the person responsible for Hedgepeth's death. They told jurors he broke into Hedgepeth's apartment, sexually assaulted her and then beat her to death.
 Defense attorneys argued that Olivares and Hedgepeth could have had consensual sex, and noted that male DNA can remain inside a woman's body for days. Defense attorney Jason Murphy also urged jurors to consider whether investigators developed tunnel vision and ignored other leads.
 Miguel Salguer Olivares on Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026 Deliberations resume Friday morning .
